findings.issue: actions/checkout leaves the default persist-credentials: true, so the GITHUB_TOKEN is written into .git/config for the rest of the job. Every later step runs dependency code: npm ci lifecycle scripts, build, tests, and the Playwright webServer. Because the token is limited to contents: read on a private repo that is already checked out, this exposes nothing new. No step pushes, so the workflow does not need the token stored.
findings.evidence: Any dependency install script or test code (repo content, i.e. already trusted committers) can read .git/config and get the token. The token has only contents:read on this repo. No reachable gain for an attacker.
findings.fix: Add `with: persist-credentials: false` to the checkout step (defence in depth).

findings.issue: All four actions are pinned to full 40-char commit SHAs with version comments, which is correct. I could not check offline that each SHA matches the tag in its comment (checkout v7.0.1, setup-node v7.1.0, cache v6.1.0, upload-artifact v7.0.2). The first real run will fail if a SHA does not exist, but it would not catch a SHA that exists on a different tag.
findings.evidence: Supply-chain hygiene only. No untrusted input path.
findings.fix: Optionally confirm with `git ls-remote https://github.com/actions/<name> refs/tags/<tag>` (or Dependabot for github-actions) when convenient.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Triggers: push and pull_request, not pull_request_target, so a fork PR never gets write tokens or secrets, and the repo is private anyway. Top-level permissions are contents: read. No secrets are referenced. No ${{ github.event.* }} or other attacker-controllable value is interpolated into run: scripts. The expressions used are github.event_name and github.ref (in concurrency only), runner.os, and a step output taken from the committed lockfile, which is used only as a cache key. Caches: the Playwright cache key is OS plus the Playwright version. GitHub's branch-scoped cache isolation stops a proof branch from poisoning main's cache. setup-node's npm cache is checked against lockfile integrity hashes by npm ci. Artifacts: only playwright-report/ is uploaded, only on e2e failure, and kept 7 days. It holds test output for the local preview build, with no env or credentials. The job has a 20-minute timeout. The two audit gates fail closed (non-zero exit fails the job). The proof-branch vulnerable packages (lodash, minimist) have no install scripts and are never merged. The README and .nvmrc changes have no security impact. Two low findings: persist-credentials (MINOR) and SHA-to-tag verification (NIT).
